_source: Transcribed VERBATIM 2026-09-05 from Projects/apps/hunter/src/reference-data/us-equity-calendar.ts (BASELINE_CLOSED_DATES + BASELINE_EARLY_CLOSES), which is itself Hunter's versioned encoding of NYSE's official 2026-2028 hours-and-calendars publication.
_why_a_table_and_not_a_formula: Hunter's own comment: 'This table is deliberately explicit. It is the versioned schedule encoded from NYSE's official 2026-2028 hours-and-calendars publication, not a holiday formula.' Good Friday and observed-weekend-holiday rules are not derivable safely. Never replace this with computed dates.
_drift_check: If Hunter's _version string changes, re-transcribe this file rather than editing it in place. Two copies of a calendar that disagree is worse than one that is stale and known to be.
_expiry: This calendar ENDS 2028-12-31. The collector MUST refuse to run, loudly, for any date after that rather than guessing. A silent fallback to a weekday check would collect on Christmas.
_early_close_note: A 13:00 ET close does not stop the 17:30 ET collection run - the session is still complete by then. But volume on an early-close day is structurally ~half a normal session, which will look like a volume anomaly to any detector calibrated on this data. Every row collected on these dates MUST carry early_close: true so calibration can control for it. This is a field that costs nothing now and is impossible to add retroactively.
_labor_day_2026: 2026-09-07 is in closed_dates, matching the brief's explicit note. Verified against Hunter's transcription and against hunter/src/providers/robinhood-acceptance-pilot-2026-09-05.ts, which states: 'Labor Day 2026-09-07 is a market holiday; the next expected session is 2026-09-08.'
